instructions:
You are controlling Mario in Super Mario Bros. World 1-2. Reach the flag alive by choosing the next controller action from the current game state. On visible continuous floor with no nearby enemy, wall or gap, advance right; a vertical jump or retreat makes no progress. Slow down or jump when the observed geometry calls for it.

The observation describes Mario's position, feet height, grounded status, motion and velocity; nearby enemies; wall geometry; floor gaps and landing surfaces; headroom; the previous action and whether jump is held. Pixel y increases downward. A smaller surface top_y is higher. Positive enemy dx is ahead; negative dx is behind. Positive vertical velocity means descending. Missing information is unknown. Use these measured facts together rather than treating one number as an action instruction.

Right/left control horizontal motion. B increases running speed and jump reach. A starts a jump only with support and a fresh press; holding A during ascent can extend height, but cannot create a new midair jump. Releasing A allows a shorter jump and prepares a later jump. The fixed controller provides one release frame when grounded with A already held and you select another jump. It does not choose when or where to jump for you. Actions normally last four native frames, with an earlier observation on landing.

Look ahead before approaching enemies, walls or missing floor. A live enemy ahead at Mario's height takes priority over clear floor. Start a jump while horizontal space remains when the jump path is clear. When an enemy approaches beyond raised tiles, consider jumping before entering the tile span; waiting to pass beneath every tile can leave no safe jump window. An overhead tile can shorten ascent, but a tile still ahead is not a reason to keep running into an enemy. When grounded with a live same-height enemy about 10 frames from contact, running right is unsafe even if the floor continues. A missing headroom measurement is unknown, not evidence of a ceiling. Check a reported obstacle's vertical extent against Mario's body and the terrain columns: an isolated tile overhead with empty space beneath it can be passed under and does not require a jump by itself. If Mario is on a raised surface and continuous lower floor is visible beyond its edge, run off and land on that floor before starting another jump, unless a visible hazard intersects the drop. Jump while support remains and close enough that the landing area will still be supported; avoid jumping so early that you descend into a later hazard. During ascent, preserve needed height and horizontal reach. During descent, consider whether the landing area is supported and safe. Walking off a gap cannot be rescued by pressing jump after support is lost. If blocked, reconsider the visible geometry and your motion instead of blindly repeating the same input.

Choose the action best suited to this current situation. Learned reflection notes are hypotheses that can be wrong; prefer current physical evidence. Do not follow a memorized coordinate route or elapsed-time button script. Return one of the offered action IDs.

criteria.right_run: Hold Right and B; release A. Use on supported floor when no immediate hazard is ahead. This action keeps Mario at floor height and cannot jump over an approaching enemy. If a live same-height enemy is closing, choose a moving jump while space remains; continuous floor does not make this action safe. An isolated overhead tile with empty space beneath it is passable. When standing on a raised surface with continuous lower floor immediately beyond its edge, run off and land on that floor if the drop is safe.
criteria.right_run_jump: Hold Right, B and A for a needed moving jump. When grounded with a live same-height enemy closing ahead, jump while space remains. If contact is approaching in roughly 10–20 frames and raised tiles lie farther ahead, consider jumping before entering their span rather than running beneath all of them. Also jump when a solid ground-level wall or pipe blocks forward travel, or shortly before a floor gap with a visible landing bank. Keep A held during ascent when height is needed. A floating tile with open space beneath it is not a ground-level wall. If Mario stands on a raised surface and continuous lower floor extends from its edge, run off and land on that floor before choosing a jump for a later gap. Pressing A while already falling cannot start a new jump.
criteria.right: Hold only Right; release both B and A. Advance at lower speed when a careful approach or jump release is useful.
criteria.right_jump: Hold Right and A; release B. Move right through a slower jump when a visible hazard requires it.
criteria.left: Hold only Left; release both B and A. Brake or retreat when continuing right would be unsafe.
criteria.left_jump: Hold Left and A; release B. Use only when an immediate visible hazard makes moving right unsafe and jumping while retreating provides a safe path. On an open route to the right, this action slows or reverses progress. If already airborne with A held, it cannot start another jump.
criteria.wait: Release all buttons to stop or let Mario settle when movement would be unsafe.
criteria.jump: Hold only A; release Left, Right and B. Use a jump in place only when a visible immediate hazard makes horizontal movement unsafe and rising helps avoid it. This action gives no rightward acceleration. On clear continuous floor it leaves Mario at the same x; choose a right-moving action. While airborne it cannot start a new jump.

If you started this retreat, continue until the lower passage is reached even if retreating takes you left of the stated range; use last_action and retreat_origin_support_feet_y as evidence.

Hint pit-takeoff: consider this near world x=1260..1325. The pit begins at1280. If grounded here, jump right NOW. If rising hold jump. If falling continue right without jump.

Hint plant-cycle-wait: consider this near world x=1390..1490. Approach the plant section cautiously. If a visible piranha_plant is extended into the path, wait on safe supported ground or retreat until it withdraws; use its current relative position and observed vertical motion to judge a safe opening. Then continue right. Do not wait for a hidden countdown: no note timer is supplied. This replaces the old timed waiting lesson and is an untested observation-based hypothesis.
